first_impression: Clean and reasonably tasteful, but it feels like a nicely designed quiz stretched far longer than the payoff deserves.
problems: The first comparison takes 7 seconds before moving on, which is too slow for a simple nutrition fact.
The countdown mechanic repeats three times and becomes predictable instead of suspenseful.
There are no actual food visuals, so the post feels abstract and less appetizing than a food brand post should.
Some type is too small, especially the USDA/source lines and explanatory callouts.
The cover does not clearly show the three matchups or promise enough payoff to stop a fast scroll.
The final summary is useful but arrives very late after repeated animations.
The RecipeFix caption makes the post feel like disguised product marketing rather than a native food-fact post.
fixes: Cut each matchup to 2-3 seconds total: show the question, quick beat, then reveal the winner immediately.
Remove the 3-2-1 countdowns or use one fast tap-style reveal instead.
Add real cutout photos or simple illustrated food icons for orange, pepper, banana, potato, ketchup and cola.
Make the winning number the visual hero and reduce secondary copy to one short line.
Put all three questions on the opening frame, e.g. 'Which has more: vitamin C, potassium, sugar?'
Move the source to the final slide only and make it legible enough to read without pausing.
Shorten the whole video to about 10-12 seconds.
If promoting RecipeFix, make the CTA softer and separate from the nutrition quiz, or remove it from this caption entirely.
